Each use case is tagged as terrestrial, space-based or hybrid, with core technologies and dated references, written to support evaluation of LEO satcom providers.

REFERENCE BRIEF

Government (non-military) telecommunications use cases

Terrestrial, space-based and hybrid communications, with technical references

33 use cases in 14 domains • 64 dated, clickable references

Prepared 28 October 2026 • Links checked 28 October 2026

Scope: civil government, public safety, transport, health, education and science. Military and defence use is excluded. Written for evaluation of LEO satcom (Starlink, Amazon Leo, Eutelsat OneWeb, Telesat Lightspeed, Viasat) and terrestrial offerings to US and European government customers.

1. Executive summary

Civil government relies on telecommunications for 14 broad mission areas. This brief catalogues 33 distinct use cases and tags each one as Terrestrial (T), Space (S) or Hybrid (H). Each entry lists the core technologies, example programmes and agencies, and authoritative references (standards, regulator or agency pages, and technical papers).

  • Hybrid is now the norm. Most government missions combine terrestrial networks for capacity with satellite for coverage, resilience and rapid deployment. 3GPP NTN (Rel-17 onward) and the FCC Supplemental Coverage from Space framework bring satellites into the same standards and regulatory regimes as mobile networks.
  • Public safety is moving to broadband. TETRA, P25 and other narrowband LMR are being replaced or complemented by 3GPP mission-critical services (MCPTT/MCVideo/MCData) on dedicated or prioritised LTE/5G (FirstNet, UK ESN). Satellite backhaul for deployables is a near-term opportunity for LEO operators.
  • Sovereignty shapes European demand. EU GOVSATCOM (pooled capacity) and IRIS² (multi-orbit constellation) define how EU institutions and Member States buy secure satcom for crisis management, surveillance, diplomatic networks and critical infrastructure. Non-EU commercial LEO capacity is likely to be positioned as complementary rather than core.
  • Alerting and emergency access are regulated obligations. Cell broadcast public warning (EU-Alert under EECC Art. 110, WEA/IPAWS) and NG112/NG911 are mandated services. D2D satellite messaging is starting to extend them into coverage gaps.
  • Safety-of-life services need certification. GMDSS, Cospas-Sarsat, ATM datalink (Iris), space-based ADS-B and SBAS (EGNOS) require recognised and certified providers, so the barrier to entry is high, but these are durable government revenue lines.
  • Digital inclusion is the largest funded civil market. BEAD ($42.45B), E-Rate, Rural Health Care and EU gigabit policy fund connectivity for unserved areas, schools and clinics. LEO is an accepted technology for the hardest-to-reach locations.
  • Resilience and security are cross-cutting. GNSS timing dependence, the space threat landscape (ENISA 2025) and post-quantum migration (NIST FIPS 203/204/205, EuroQCI, Eagle-1) add requirements to every government telecom procurement.

About the links: All 64 references were checked on 28 Oct 2026. 57 loaded successfully. 2 European Commission pages block automated checks (HTTP 403), and 1 ITU page timed out. These are marked in the reference list and should be opened in a browser. 4 deep-link documents (standards PDFs, Federal Register notice) were located through search but not fetched directly. Their landing pages are verified.

3. Detailed use cases by domain

3.1 Public safety and emergency response

1. Mission-critical public safety broadband [H: Hybrid]

Dedicated or prioritised LTE/5G networks for police, fire and EMS, with priority, pre-emption, hardened cores and coverage extension. Satellite extends coverage to remote areas and serves as backhaul.

  • Typical technologies: 3GPP LTE/5G with QPP (QoS, priority, pre-emption), Band 14 (US), MCX, NTN/SCS coverage extension
  • Example programmes / agencies: FirstNet (US), UK ESN, Virve 2.0 (Finland), RRF (France)
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: LEO backhaul for deployables and remote sites; D2D/SCS (the FCC framework includes FirstNet Band 14).
  • References: [1] FirstNet Authority: The Network (NPSBN, Band 14, deployables); [5] The Emergency Services Mobile Communications Programme (ESN) (updated 17 Feb 2025); [21] Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) overview (Rel-17/18/19); [22] Single Network Future: Supplemental Coverage from Space: fact sheet and draft Report and Order (Feb 2024)

2. Mission-critical push-to-talk, video and data (MCX); TETRA/LMR interworking [T: Terrestrial]

Group voice, video and data for responders. Agencies are migrating from TETRA/TETRAPOL/P25 narrowband LMR to 3GPP MCX over broadband, using interworking gateways during the transition.

  • Typical technologies: 3GPP MCPTT/MCVideo/MCData (SA6, Rel-13+), ETSI TETRA (TC TCCE), P25, LMR–LTE interworking
  • Example programmes / agencies: ESN (UK), FirstNet Push-to-Talk, national TETRA networks (e.g. Airwave UK, BOS digital radio Germany, ASTRID Belgium)
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Satellite backhaul for TETRA base stations and MCX sites, and for deployable PTT.
  • References: [2] Mission Critical: LTE/5G MCPTT, MCVideo, MCData (SA6); [3] Mission Critical Services in 3GPP (found via search); [4] Wireless and mobile technologies: TETRA and critical communications (TC TCCE); [5] The Emergency Services Mobile Communications Programme (ESN) (updated 17 Feb 2025)

3. Deployable and transportable networks (cell-on-wheels, system-on-a-chip, drones) [H: Hybrid]

Rapidly deployed tactical cells and core networks for incidents, wildfires and events, often with satellite backhaul where terrestrial fibre or microwave is unavailable.

  • Typical technologies: Deployable LTE/5G cores (IOPS), satellite backhaul (GEO/LEO/MEO), mesh, aerial base stations
  • Example programmes / agencies: FirstNet deployable fleet, ESN, civil protection agencies
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: A primary LEO opportunity: low-latency backhaul for deployables, e.g. via Starlink, Amazon Leo, OneWeb, Telesat Lightspeed or Viasat terminals.
  • References: [1] FirstNet Authority: The Network (NPSBN, Band 14, deployables); [15] Emergency telecommunications: backgrounder (NETPs, EW4All, terrestrial and satellite networks; last updated Oct 2026); [21] Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) overview (Rel-17/18/19)

4. Next-generation emergency calling (NG911 / NG112) [T: Terrestrial]

IP-based emergency call handling that adds multimedia, text and location data, plus interconnection between PSAPs (public-safety answering points) via an ESInet.

  • Typical technologies: SIP/IMS, ESInet, NENA i3, ETSI TS 103 479 (NG112), AML/handset location, RTT, eCall
  • Example programmes / agencies: US NG911 programme, EU EECC Art. 109 implementation, EENA
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Satellite emergency-SOS gateways connect to PSAPs, and NG112 standards must handle NTN-originated calls.
  • References: [9] Next Generation 911 (NG911); [10] Technical specifications: NG112 architecture; [11] ETSI TS 103 479 V1.3.1: Core elements for network-independent access to emergency services (NG112) (found via search)

5. Public warning (cell broadcast, WEA, EU-Alert, multi-channel) [H: Hybrid]

Geo-targeted alerts to every handset in an area, alongside broadcast, sirens and apps. EU Member States must operate a public warning system under EECC Art. 110.

  • Typical technologies: 3GPP Cell Broadcast / PWS, LB-SMS, CAP, ETSI TS 102 900 (EU-Alert), WEA, IPAWS-OPEN
  • Example programmes / agencies: IPAWS/WEA (US), NL-Alert, FR-Alert, UK Emergency Alerts, ITU Early Warnings for All
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Satellite broadcast and D2D messaging can extend alerting to coverage gaps.
  • References: [12] ETSI TS 102 900 V1.4.1: Emergency Communications; European Public Warning System (EU-Alert) using cell broadcast; [13] Wireless Emergency Alerts (WEA); [14] Integrated Public Alert and Warning System (IPAWS); [15] Emergency telecommunications: backgrounder (NETPs, EW4All, terrestrial and satellite networks; last updated Oct 2026)

6. Priority telecommunications for officials (GETS/WPS and equivalents) [T: Terrestrial]

Priority call completion on public networks for national security and emergency-preparedness (NS/EP) users during congestion.

  • Typical technologies: Priority access (GETS, WPS, NGN-GETS), MPS/3GPP priority, ARP/QCI
  • Example programmes / agencies: CISA GETS/WPS (US), MTPAS-equivalent schemes in Europe
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Satellite backup for NS/EP continuity; priority on satellite networks is an emerging requirement.
  • References: [8] Government Emergency Telecommunications Service (GETS); [7] National Emergency Communications Plan (NECP); [6] SAFECOM: interoperable emergency communications

3.2 Disaster management and humanitarian response

7. Emergency satellite mapping and EO-based damage assessment [S: Space]

Rapid satellite imagery and analytics for flood, fire, earthquake and other mapping, triggered by civil protection authorities.

  • Typical technologies: Optical/SAR EO satellites, ground segments, data relay, GIS
  • Example programmes / agencies: Copernicus EMS, International Charter Space and Major Disasters, UN-SPIDER
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: LEO data relay and broadband move EO products to the field.
  • References: [18] Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS); [19] International Charter: Space and Major Disasters; [20] UN-SPIDER: space-based information for disaster management

8. Emergency telecommunications deployment (NETPs, Tampere Convention, satellite phones) [H: Hybrid]

Pre-positioned and rapidly deployed satellite terminals, satellite phones and VSATs that restore communications for responders and affected populations.

  • Typical technologies: MSS (L/S-band), VSAT/FSS, BGAN, LEO broadband kits, HF/amateur radio
  • Example programmes / agencies: ITU NETPs, Tampere Convention (50 ratifications), Emergency Telecommunications Cluster (WFP)
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Fly-away LEO kits are now standard in many responder caches.
  • References: [15] Emergency telecommunications: backgrounder (NETPs, EW4All, terrestrial and satellite networks; last updated Oct 2026); [16] Tampere Convention on the Provision of Telecommunication Resources for Disaster Mitigation and Relief Operations; [17] ITU-D Emergency Telecommunications portal (timed out on automated check)

9. Distress beacons and satellite-aided search and rescue [S: Space]

406 MHz ELT, EPIRB and PLB distress beacons detected via LEO/MEO/GEO payloads and relayed to rescue coordination centres. Galileo adds a return-link acknowledgement.

  • Typical technologies: Cospas-Sarsat LEOSAR/MEOSAR/GEOSAR, Galileo SAR return link
  • Example programmes / agencies: Cospas-Sarsat, national RCCs, EUSPA Galileo SAR
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Indirect; D2D SOS messaging complements beacons.
  • References: [27] International Cospas-Sarsat Programme (satellite-aided search and rescue); [50] Galileo

3.3 Border, coast guard and maritime

10. Vessel tracking: terrestrial and satellite AIS [H: Hybrid]

Identification and tracking of vessels for safety, fisheries control, pollution response and border surveillance. Satellite AIS extends tracking beyond the coastal VHF range.

  • Typical technologies: AIS (ITU-R M.1371-6), satellite AIS, VDES, LRIT
  • Example programmes / agencies: EMSA SafeSeaNet/CleanSeaNet, national coast guards, Frontex (via EMSA services)
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: LEO constellations host AIS/VDES payloads; broadband to patrol vessels.
  • References: [25] Recommendation ITU-R M.1371: Technical characteristics of AIS in the VHF maritime mobile band (latest: M.1371-6); [26] European Maritime Safety Agency (vessel traffic monitoring, SafeSeaNet, satellite AIS services); [64] Kodheli et al., "Satellite Communications in the New Space Era: A Survey and Future Challenges", IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials (arXiv:2002.08811)

11. Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS) [H: Hybrid]

SOLAS-mandated distress, urgency and safety communications using terrestrial VHF/MF/HF DSC and recognised mobile satellite services.

  • Typical technologies: DSC, NAVTEX, recognised GMDSS satellite providers (Inmarsat, Iridium), EPIRB
  • Example programmes / agencies: IMO, MRCCs, national coast guards
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Only recognised providers qualify. LEO broadband carries non-GMDSS crew and operations traffic.
  • References: [24] Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS); [27] International Cospas-Sarsat Programme (satellite-aided search and rescue)

12. Border and maritime surveillance communications [S: Space]

Secure beyond-line-of-sight links for patrol vessels, aircraft, drones and remote border posts.

  • Typical technologies: GOVSATCOM pooled capacity, secure satcom, UAS C2 links
  • Example programmes / agencies: EU GOVSATCOM (border and maritime surveillance listed use case), IRIS², coast guards
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Governed by sovereignty and security accreditation; multi-orbit services.
  • References: [33] GOVSATCOM: EU governmental satellite communications; [32] IRIS²: EU secure connectivity programme

3.4 Civil aviation and air traffic management

13. Satellite datalink for air traffic management (ATM) [S: Space]

Satellite-based controller–pilot datalink and 4D trajectory exchange that supplement congested VHF datalink.

  • Typical technologies: Iris (ESA/Inmarsat SATCOM datalink), ATN/IPS, SESAR
  • Example programmes / agencies: ESA Iris, SESAR JU, EUROCONTROL, ANSPs
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Future multi-link ATM may include LEO, subject to safety certification.
  • References: [28] Iris: satellite communications for air traffic management; [29] SESAR Joint Undertaking (Single European Sky ATM Research)

14. Surveillance: ADS-B including space-based ADS-B [H: Hybrid]

Aircraft broadcast GNSS-derived positions, received by ground stations and, through space-based ADS-B, over oceans and polar regions.

  • Typical technologies: 1090ES/UAT ADS-B, Iridium NEXT hosted ADS-B receivers (Aireon)
  • Example programmes / agencies: FAA, NAV CANADA, NATS, other ANSPs
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Space-based ADS-B is an established LEO hosted-payload use case.
  • References: [30] Automatic Dependent Surveillance–Broadcast (ADS-B); [31] Aireon: space-based ADS-B (Iridium NEXT hosted payloads); [64] Kodheli et al., "Satellite Communications in the New Space Era: A Survey and Future Challenges", IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials (arXiv:2002.08811)

15. Satellite-based augmentation for precision approach (SBAS) [S: Space]

GNSS augmentation that enables LPV approaches and integrity for aviation and other safety-of-life users.

  • Typical technologies: EGNOS (GEO), WAAS, SBAS safety-of-life service
  • Example programmes / agencies: EUSPA EGNOS, FAA WAAS
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Not a LEO comms use case. LEO PNT augmentation is emerging.
  • References: [51] EGNOS (European SBAS); [50] Galileo

3.5 Government connectivity, sovereignty and continuity

16. Sovereign secure governmental satellite communications [S: Space]

Secure, resilient satcom for civil government users (crisis management, surveillance, key infrastructure), with pooling and sharing of capacity.

  • Typical technologies: GOVSATCOM pooled GEO/LEO capacity, IRIS² (multi-orbit LEO+MEO), encryption, ground segment hubs
  • Example programmes / agencies: EU GOVSATCOM, IRIS² (SpaceRISE consortium), national programmes
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Commercial LEO capacity complements IRIS². Sovereignty rules shape eligibility.
  • References: [33] GOVSATCOM: EU governmental satellite communications; [32] IRIS²: EU secure connectivity programme; [63] ENISA Space Threat Landscape 2025 (26 Mar 2025)

17. Continuity of government (COOP) and resilient backup links [H: Hybrid]

Diverse-path WAN for ministries, agencies and critical sites: terrestrial primary with satellite (LEO/GEO) failover, plus priority services.

  • Typical technologies: SD-WAN with multi-orbit satellite, GETS/WPS, NECP planning
  • Example programmes / agencies: CISA NECP, national resilience programmes
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: A key LEO use case: SD-WAN failover via Starlink, Amazon Leo, OneWeb, Telesat or Viasat.
  • References: [7] National Emergency Communications Plan (NECP); [8] Government Emergency Telecommunications Service (GETS); [21] Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) overview (Rel-17/18/19)

18. Diplomatic and embassy networks [H: Hybrid]

Secure connectivity for embassies, consulates and missions abroad, including in places where host-nation networks are unreliable or untrusted.

  • Typical technologies: Encrypted IP over leased lines and satellite, GOVSATCOM/IRIS² secure services, PQC migration
  • Example programmes / agencies: Foreign ministries, EEAS; GOVSATCOM/IRIS² list diplomatic networks among use cases
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Sovereign/secure satcom and hardened LEO terminals.
  • References: [33] GOVSATCOM: EU governmental satellite communications; [32] IRIS²: EU secure connectivity programme; [59] Post-Quantum Cryptography (FIPS 203/204/205)

3.6 Digital inclusion: rural broadband, education and e-health

19. Rural and remote broadband (universal service) [H: Hybrid]

Public funding to close coverage gaps with fibre, fixed wireless and satellite, including LEO for the hardest-to-reach locations.

  • Typical technologies: FTTH, FWA, LEO broadband, mobile 4G/5G
  • Example programmes / agencies: NTIA BEAD ($42.45B), EU Gigabit Infrastructure Act and national broadband plans
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: LEO is an eligible BEAD technology; national schemes use voucher models.
  • References: [34] Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment (BEAD) Program; [35] Gigabit Infrastructure Act (blocks automated check); [64] Kodheli et al., "Satellite Communications in the New Space Era: A Survey and Future Challenges", IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials (arXiv:2002.08811)

20. School and library connectivity [H: Hybrid]

Connectivity for schools and libraries funded by subsidies or donor programmes; satellite reaches remote schools.

  • Typical technologies: Fibre, FWA, satellite (GEO/LEO), Wi-Fi
  • Example programmes / agencies: FCC E-Rate (US), UNICEF–ITU Giga
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: LEO for remote schools (Giga projects).
  • References: [36] E-Rate: Schools and Libraries USF Program; [38] Giga: connecting every school to the Internet

21. Telehealth and rural health care [H: Hybrid]

Connectivity for rural clinics, telemedicine, remote diagnostics and health-data exchange.

  • Typical technologies: Broadband (fibre, FWA, satellite), secure health networks, IoT medical devices
  • Example programmes / agencies: FCC Rural Health Care Program, US DOT ITS4US (HIRTA health-transport connector), national e-health agencies
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: LEO for remote clinics and mobile health units.
  • References: [37] Rural Health Care Program; [45] ITS Joint Program Office (V2X Accelerator; Sep 2026 update); [32] IRIS²: EU secure connectivity programme

3.7 Smart cities, IoT and utilities

22. Municipal IoT (metering, lighting, waste, environmental sensors) [T: Terrestrial]

Low-power wide-area sensor networks for city services and public infrastructure monitoring.

  • Typical technologies: NB-IoT, LTE-M, LoRaWAN, 5G RedCap
  • Example programmes / agencies: Municipal smart-city programmes
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Limited LEO relevance, mainly backhaul.
  • References: [39] Mobile IoT (NB-IoT and LTE-M, licensed LPWA); [40] LoRa Alliance (LoRaWAN specifications)

23. Smart grid and utility communications [H: Hybrid]

Communications for grid monitoring, protection, distribution automation and AMI (smart metering), with strict reliability and timing needs.

  • Typical technologies: Private LTE (e.g. 450 MHz in Europe), fibre, PLC, satellite for remote substations, NIST interoperability framework
  • Example programmes / agencies: Utilities, NIST Smart Grid Program, energy regulators
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Satellite backup for remote substations and renewables.
  • References: [41] Smart Grid (NIST Smart Grid Interoperability Framework); [39] Mobile IoT (NB-IoT and LTE-M, licensed LPWA); [52] NIST Time Services (UTC(NIST) distribution: Internet time, WWV/WWVB, etc.)

24. Satellite IoT for remote assets [S: Space]

Monitoring of remote infrastructure, water, pipelines, wildlife and agriculture beyond terrestrial coverage.

  • Typical technologies: 3GPP IoT-NTN (NB-IoT/LTE-M over satellite, Rel-17+), proprietary LEO IoT
  • Example programmes / agencies: Environment and water agencies, agriculture ministries
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: D2D IoT is a growing LEO niche.
  • References: [21] Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) overview (Rel-17/18/19); [64] Kodheli et al., "Satellite Communications in the New Space Era: A Survey and Future Challenges", IEEE Communications Surveys & Tutorials (arXiv:2002.08811)

3.8 Transportation

25. Railway mobile communications (GSM-R to FRMCS) [T: Terrestrial]

Train control (ETCS L2/L3), voice and data for railway operations. FRMCS (5G-based) succeeds GSM-R, which is expected to become obsolete around 2035.

  • Typical technologies: GSM-R, FRMCS (3GPP 5G, MCX), ETSI TC RT, 1900 MHz/900 MHz harmonised bands
  • Example programmes / agencies: UIC, EU rail infrastructure managers, CCS TSI
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: FRMCS anticipates satellite bearers for low-density lines.
  • References: [42] FRMCS: Future Railway Mobile Communication System; [43] FRMCS System Requirements Specification AT-7800 v2.1.0 (PDF) (found via search); [44] Automotive and Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS, C-ITS; TC RT for railway telecoms)

26. Cooperative intelligent transport systems (C-ITS / V2X) [T: Terrestrial]

Vehicle-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-infrastructure messaging for road safety, work zones and traffic management.

  • Typical technologies: ITS-G5 / C-V2X (PC5, 5.9 GHz), ETSI ITS, SAE J2735
  • Example programmes / agencies: US DOT V2X Accelerator, C-Roads (EU), road authorities
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Limited; satellite supports positioning and connected-vehicle telematics.
  • References: [44] Automotive and Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS, C-ITS; TC RT for railway telecoms); [45] ITS Joint Program Office (V2X Accelerator; Sep 2026 update)

3.9 Environment, weather and Earth observation

27. Meteorological data collection and exchange [H: Hybrid]

Global exchange of observations and forecasts between national meteorological services, and satellite data dissemination.

  • Typical technologies: WMO WIS 2.0 (operational since Jan 2025), GTS, EUMETCast, DCS (data collection platforms)
  • Example programmes / agencies: WMO, EUMETSAT, NOAA, national meteorological services
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Remote weather stations backhauled over LEO and IoT-NTN.
  • References: [46] WMO Information System (WIS 2.0); [47] EUMETSAT (meteorological satellites and data dissemination)

28. EO data relay and downlink [S: Space]

High-throughput relay of EO data from LEO satellites through GEO laser terminals, reducing latency for time-critical services.

  • Typical technologies: EDRS optical inter-satellite links (1.8 Gbit/s), optical ground stations
  • Example programmes / agencies: ESA EDRS (SpaceDataHighway), Copernicus Sentinels
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Optical ISLs in LEO constellations are converging with relay services.
  • References: [48] European Data Relay System (EDRS): overview; [18] Copernicus Emergency Management Service (CEMS)

3.10 Positioning, navigation and timing (PNT)

29. GNSS timing for telecom and critical infrastructure, plus PNT resilience [H: Hybrid]

GNSS-derived timing synchronises mobile networks, grids and finance. Governments mandate resilience against jamming and spoofing through terrestrial backups.

  • Typical technologies: GPS, Galileo, EGNOS, PTP/SyncE, UTC(NIST) time services, eLoran/fibre time
  • Example programmes / agencies: GPS.gov, EUSPA, NIST, CISA, DHS S&T
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: LEO PNT is an emerging complement. Galileo/GPS remain the baseline.
  • References: [49] GPS.gov: official US government information about GPS; [50] Galileo; [51] EGNOS (European SBAS); [52] NIST Time Services (UTC(NIST) distribution: Internet time, WWV/WWVB, etc.); [53] Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (resilient PNT, Federal PNT Services Acquisitions Guidance); [54] Best Practices for Resilient PNT Supporting Critical Infrastructure (PDF dated 20 Feb 2025)

3.11 Law enforcement and justice

30. Lawful interception and law-enforcement communications [H: Hybrid]

Standardised interfaces for court-authorised interception across fixed, mobile and satellite networks, plus secure LE radio and data.

  • Typical technologies: ETSI TC LI standards, TETRA/MCX, 3GPP NTN regulatory requirements
  • Example programmes / agencies: National police, interior ministries, ETSI TC LI
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: Satellite and D2D operators must support national LI obligations, including landing rights.
  • References: [55] Lawful Interception (ETSI TC LI standards); [4] Wireless and mobile technologies: TETRA and critical communications (TC TCCE); [21] Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) overview (Rel-17/18/19)

3.12 Scientific and space agency communications

31. Space communications networks (deep space, near Earth, relay) [S: Space]

Ground and space relay networks that support civil science missions, crewed spaceflight and commercial service procurement.

  • Typical technologies: NASA SCaN (DSN, Near Space Network), ESA EDRS, optical communications
  • Example programmes / agencies: NASA SCaN, ESA
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: NASA is shifting near-Earth relay toward commercial services.
  • References: [56] Space Communications and Navigation (SCaN) Program; [48] European Data Relay System (EDRS): overview

3.13 Direct-to-device (D2D) satellite services

32. D2D emergency messaging and supplemental coverage from space [H: Hybrid]

Satellite connectivity to unmodified or NTN-capable handsets, including SOS, text and later voice/data, in partnership with mobile operators.

  • Typical technologies: 3GPP NTN (Rel-17/18/19), FCC SCS framework, MSS/MNO spectrum sharing
  • Example programmes / agencies: FCC SCS (GN Docket 23-65), MNO partnerships with Starlink, AST SpaceMobile, Amazon Leo, etc.
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: A core LEO opportunity. WRC-27 is studying MSS/IMT D2D spectrum.
  • References: [21] Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) overview (Rel-17/18/19); [22] Single Network Future: Supplemental Coverage from Space: fact sheet and draft Report and Order (Feb 2024); [23] Single Network Future: Supplemental Coverage from Space (final rule, Federal Register, 30 Apr 2024) (found via search)

3.14 Quantum-secure communications

33. Quantum key distribution and post-quantum cryptography migration [H: Hybrid]

Protection of government communications against future quantum attacks, through terrestrial and space-based QKD and migration to NIST PQC algorithms.

  • Typical technologies: Terrestrial fibre QKD, space QKD (Eagle-1), PQC (FIPS 203/204/205)
  • Example programmes / agencies: EuroQCI (EU), ESA Eagle-1 (launch planned late 2026/early 2027), NIST PQC
  • Satellite / LEO relevance: IRIS² integrates with EuroQCI. LEO operators face PQC migration requirements.
  • References: [57] European Quantum Communication Infrastructure (EuroQCI) (blocks automated check); [58] Eagle-1: European space-based QKD mission; [59] Post-Quantum Cryptography (FIPS 203/204/205)

4. Cross-cutting considerations

4.1 Spectrum

Government services rely on harmonised spectrum: PPDR bands (e.g. Band 14 in the US, 700 MHz/450 MHz in Europe), rail (FRMCS 900/1900 MHz), ITS (5.9 GHz), aeronautical and maritime safety bands, and satellite allocations (L/S-band MSS, Ku/Ka/Q/V FSS). D2D satellite use of terrestrial mobile spectrum is governed nationally (FCC SCS framework) and is under international study for WRC-27. CEPT ECC decisions set European harmonisation. 3GPP has defined NTN bands for satellite access (e.g. n255/n256 L/S-band, with Ka-band NTN in later releases).

Key references: [60] Radio Regulations (2024 edition); [61] Electronic Communications Committee (ECC): spectrum harmonisation decisions and reports; [22] Single Network Future: Supplemental Coverage from Space: fact sheet and draft Report and Order (Feb 2024); [21] Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) overview (Rel-17/18/19); [62] Global Satellite Operators Association (GSOA)

4.2 Security and sovereignty

Civil governments increasingly require accredited, sovereign-controlled services: EU GOVSATCOM security requirements, IRIS² governmental services, landing rights and lawful interception obligations, supply-chain controls and data localisation. ENISA’s Space Threat Landscape (2025) catalogues threats to ground, space and user segments. Quantum-safe migration (NIST FIPS 203/204/205; NIST IR 8547 targets deprecating vulnerable algorithms by 2035) and EuroQCI/Eagle-1 QKD shape long-term cryptographic requirements.

Key references: [33] GOVSATCOM: EU governmental satellite communications; [32] IRIS²: EU secure connectivity programme; [63] ENISA Space Threat Landscape 2025 (26 Mar 2025); [59] Post-Quantum Cryptography (FIPS 203/204/205); [57] European Quantum Communication Infrastructure (EuroQCI); [55] Lawful Interception (ETSI TC LI standards)

4.3 Resilience and continuity

Requirements include path and orbit diversity (terrestrial plus GEO/LEO/MEO), priority services (GETS/WPS), hardened deployables, power autonomy, and PNT resilience against GNSS jamming and spoofing. National emergency communications plans and ITU NETPs set the planning frameworks.

Key references: [7] National Emergency Communications Plan (NECP); [8] Government Emergency Telecommunications Service (GETS); [53] Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (resilient PNT, Federal PNT Services Acquisitions Guidance); [54] Best Practices for Resilient PNT Supporting Critical Infrastructure (PDF dated 20 Feb 2025); [15] Emergency telecommunications: backgrounder (NETPs, EW4All, terrestrial and satellite networks; last updated Oct 2026)

4.4 Interoperability and standards

Cross-agency and cross-border interoperability depends on 3GPP MCX, TETRA/LMR interworking gateways, NG112/NG911 (ESInet, ETSI TS 103 479), CAP-based alerting (EU-Alert, IPAWS), 3GPP NTN integration of satellite into mobile cores, and SAFECOM governance guidance.

Key references: [6] SAFECOM: interoperable emergency communications; [2] Mission Critical: LTE/5G MCPTT, MCVideo, MCData (SA6); [21] Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) overview (Rel-17/18/19); [10] Technical specifications: NG112 architecture; [12] ETSI TS 102 900 V1.4.1: Emergency Communications; European Public Warning System (EU-Alert) using cell broadcast

4.5 Procurement and funding models

Typical routes are: national public-safety network concessions (FirstNet, ESN); subsidy and universal-service programmes (BEAD, E-Rate, Rural Health Care); EU pooling and sharing (GOVSATCOM Hub) and the IRIS² public–private partnership; and framework contracts for satcom and SD-WAN. Procurement rules increasingly add resilience, PNT, cybersecurity and sovereignty clauses, for example CISA’s Federal PNT Services Acquisitions Guidance. Vendors should expect technology-neutral tenders with explicit security accreditation and service-level requirements.

Key references: [34] Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment (BEAD) Program; [36] E-Rate: Schools and Libraries USF Program; [37] Rural Health Care Program; [33] GOVSATCOM: EU governmental satellite communications; [32] IRIS²: EU secure connectivity programme; [53] Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (resilient PNT, Federal PNT Services Acquisitions Guidance)
